metadata.title: PISA 2022 RESULTS (VOLUME III): FACTSHEETS – UNITED ARAB EMIRATES

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for the United Arab Emirates using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database tables. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD tables typically incorporate sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each participating country/economy. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used, so the weighting implementation details are not recoverable from the provided text. Because this is a descriptive results factsheet rather than an author-reestimated microdata analysis, the appropriate weights are those already applied in the OECD’s published PISA database tables.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because the provided text is a descriptive factsheet summarizing published PISA 2022 creative thinking scores and related percentages from OECD tables, rather than reporting an author-led PV estimation procedure. Missing-data handling is not reported in the factsheet excerpt because it does not describe the microdata processing or imputation/deletion rules used to construct the published estimates. This omission is expected for a country factsheet that points to OECD database tables and technical documentation elsewhere (e.g., Reader’s Guide and annexes).

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PISA 2022 United Arab Emirates sample of 15-year-old students who completed the creative thinking assessment (reported as 24,600 students in 840 schools). The factsheet indicates that these students completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science and that the creative thinking results are reported for the creative thinking test implementation in the United Arab Emirates.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet reports creative thinking results for 15-year-old students in the United Arab Emirates on a 60-point scale. It summarizes overall performance relative to the OECD average, the share of students reaching baseline proficiency (Level 3) and top proficiency (Levels 5–6), and relative strengths across ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) and domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). The factsheet also reports within-country performance gaps by socio-economic quartiles and gender, and it links creative thinking to mathematics and reading performance using reported correlations and variance decomposition (e.g., 40% of creative thinking variation uniquely attributed to mathematics performance in the UAE). It further presents associations between creative thinking and students’ beliefs/attitudes, school pedagogies, and digital tool use, while noting that PISA’s technical standards and COVID-19-related implementation issues may affect interpretability for some countries/economies (asterisk notation).
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a descriptive OECD PISA country factsheet rather than an empirical ML study with an author-specified predictive modeling pipeline. As a result, there are no author-trained machine learning models, no reported PV estimation procedure, and no author-level missing-data handling strategy to extract from the provided text. The extraction therefore focuses on the assessment design and reported benchmarks, leaving ML-specific fields empty by design.
